name: DVB-T digital television (signalling)
label: DVB-T
notes: DVB-T terrestrial television, signalling only: the external dvbt-rx (a separate GPL program the operator builds: a small wrapper, not yet published, around the modemdvb receiver of SDRangel, which the install pointer names) locks to one multiplex and reports what it signals about itself: the channel width it locked at (8, 7, 6 and 5 MHz are tried in turn), 2K or 8K carriers, guard interval, constellation, code rate, hierarchy and the cell id when the multiplex sends one (many do not: cell_id is then null). No picture, sound or service names yet. Identify and classify offer the row between 174 and 862 MHz, the broadcast bands DVB-T is used in across regions; a job started by hand runs anywhere. Centre the job on the measured middle of the multiplex with a band that covers it; the capture must be at least as wide. An event comes when lock is gained or lost and every 2 s while locked; locked false means no DVB-T multiplex was found at any width (DVB-T2 is not looked for). offset_hz is the multiplex's carrier offset from the job's centre and clock_ppm the sample clock error, both as the receiver measured them; snr_db is the mean error of the equalised pilot carriers, unweighted, so carriers in a fade drag it down: a strong multiplex with multipath reads low, even below 0 dB while locked, and it is not the level over the noise floor. ripple_db is the spread of the channel's response across the multiplex (a few dB is flat, tens is multipath or a second site of a same-frequency network). resyncs counts timing jumps recovered without losing lock since the last acquisition, usually samples lost on the way in. The node hands the program the capture unfiltered when the band is most of it (the job's context says filter none); dvbt-rx low-passes to the width it tries itself, so neighbouring multiplexes do not reach the receiver.
